cohort: Singleton pregnancies above 34 weeks gestation, giving birth either by instrumental-assisted delivery or cesarean section in labor
finding: While cesarean section in labor was associated with lower rates of severe anemia and hemorrhage in mothers, and lower cord pH in neonates, instrumental-assisted vaginal delivery did not differ significantly in other neonatal outcomes and may be a viable alternative to cesarean section.
mod_finding: This study compared neonatal and maternal outcomes for instrumental-assisted vaginal delivery and cesarean section during labor, finding that instrumental-assisted delivery can be a safe alternative to cesarean section.
